nodes.name: Desert sunlight
nodes.desc: Intense sun powers desert plants, but heat sends many animals underground for the day.

nodes.name: Scarce rainfall
nodes.desc: Rain is scarce and irregular; the park lost roughly 39% of its annual precipitation between 1895 and 2016, and plants and animals depend on it.

nodes.name: Winter cold
nodes.desc: Joshua tree blooming depends on timely rain and a winter freeze.

nodes.name: Springs and oases
nodes.desc: Natural oases, springs and seeps are rare water sources vital to resident wildlife, and support the native fan palm.

nodes.name: Soil microbes and fungi
nodes.desc: Break down dead plants and animals, returning nutrients to the sparse desert soil.

nodes.name: Creosote bush
nodes.desc: Typical shrub of the lower desert. Desert tortoises and chuckwallas eat it, and tortoises get much of their water from such plants.

nodes.name: Joshua tree
nodes.desc: The park namesake, dominant in the open Mojave areas. Pollinated by yucca moths, its seeds are moved by ground squirrels.

nodes.name: Cholla cactus
nodes.desc: A spiny cactus of the lower desert whose pads and fruit are food for tortoises and other desert animals.

nodes.name: California fan palm
nodes.desc: The only palm native to California; grows in the park only at oases with year-round water.

nodes.name: Desert tortoise
nodes.desc: Threatened grazer that eats grasses, wildflowers and cactus and spends most of its life in burrows. Ravens take juveniles.

nodes.name: Merriam's kangaroo rat
nodes.desc: A seed-eating rodent that shelters underground by day. Coyotes, hawks and snakes prey on it.

nodes.name: White-tailed antelope squirrel
nodes.desc: A daytime ground squirrel of dry scrub that eats seeds and plants. Hawks and coyotes prey on it.

nodes.name: Black-tailed jackrabbit
nodes.desc: Browses desert shrubs and cacti and is a main meal for coyotes and hawks.

nodes.name: Desert bighorn sheep
nodes.desc: The park service reports healthy herds in the park. Grazes on shrubs and cacti and is prey for coyotes.

nodes.name: Yucca moth
nodes.desc: Pollinates Joshua trees while laying eggs in the flowers; its larvae eat some of the seeds.

nodes.name: California harvester ant
nodes.desc: Gathers seeds of desert plants for its nest and is prey for horned lizards.

nodes.name: Desert horned lizard
nodes.desc: A flat-bodied lizard of sandy desert that eats mainly ants and is prey for hawks and roadrunners.

nodes.name: Sidewinder
nodes.desc: A small desert rattlesnake that hunts rodents and lizards. Coyotes and hawks eat it.

nodes.name: Greater roadrunner
nodes.desc: Fast ground bird that hunts lizards, snakes, rodents and insects.

nodes.name: Common raven
nodes.desc: Omnivore and scavenger; thought to take many young desert tortoises, especially near towns.

nodes.name: Turkey vulture
nodes.desc: Scans the desert from the air and from rock perches for carrion.

nodes.name: Coyote
nodes.desc: Dusk- and night-active predator of rodents, rabbits, reptiles and bighorn sheep that also scavenges and eats fruit.

nodes.name: Red-tailed hawk
nodes.desc: A daytime raptor that hunts rodents, rabbits, lizards, snakes and even ravens in open desert country.
